grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.rule: いきません。いかないみちです。

tables.caption: Polite negative → plain negative. Whole taught pairs; English meanings in the grammar note.
Polite negative → plain negative / noun modifier. Translations in the grammar note.
rows: あんぜんではありません
あんぜんではないみち
べんりではありません

tables.caption: Noun identification and absence are different; translations in the grammar note.

grammar.note_en:
A plain negative says that something does not happen, or will not happen, without the polite ます ending. A noun-modifying clause is a short description before a noun: いかないみち means “a road one does not take.” The whole sentence may still end politely. Main narration and service encounters remain polite here. The bounded whole pairs are いきません → いかない, “do not go”; つかいません → つかわない, “do not use”; もちません → もたない, “do not hold/carry”; とおりません → とおらない, “do not pass along”; おきません → おかない, “do not put down”; わたりません → わたらない, “do not cross.” Do not replace ます mechanically with ない. These verbs change different parts of their ending. Learn the displayed pairs. Plain affirmative とおる/わたる/つかう/かえる mean pass along/cross/use/return in the same bounded descriptions. They do not introduce plain past.

An i-adjective ends in い. Its negative changes final い to くない. Here あぶない “dangerous” becomes あぶなくない “not dangerous”; とおい “far” becomes とおくない “not far”; ちかい “near” becomes ちかくない “not near”; せまい “cramped/narrow” becomes せまくない “not narrow.” Add です for a polite statement, as in とおくないです, “it is not far.” Before a noun, omit です: あぶなくないみち is “a road that is not dangerous.” These are first taught negatives, not forms assumed from the earlier room chapter. Do not infer adjective past forms yet.

A na-adjective uses な in affirmative noun modification: あんぜんなみち, “a safe road.” Its negative uses ではない: あんぜんではないみち, “a road that is not safe.” The polite negative statement is あんぜんではありません, “it is not safe.” べんりではありません means “it is not convenient”; this polite negative is the form used in this story. In these negative modifiers, do not add な after ない. ない already supplies the negative ending. The convenient-looking shorter route cannot be used merely because it is near.

A noun can also have a plain negative predicate: はしではない, “it is not a bridge.” はしではないです gives the polite version used here; the earlier はしではありません is also polite. This identifies what an object is not. It differs from はしがありません, “there is no bridge.” The bounded negative existence description はしがないところ means “a place where there is no bridge.” It describes an absence, not a negative instruction. None of these forms teaches negative requests, plain past, permission, potential or a conditional construction.

A line on an old map is evidence to compare, not proof that a bridge exists today or that it once existed. The characters observe a barrier and an absent crossing, then label their working copy and a separate memo. They do not amend the old wet original. The remembered river shape does not reveal the map's author, owner or date. Authored readings support decoding of familiar spellings; English meanings in the pre-reading packet supply meaning before new words occur. No new kanji character is required in this chapter; the stage ceilings are not character quotas.

notes: Original fictional contemporary Japanese narrative, diagrams, practice and explanations. No authentic quotation, private correspondence or audio.

Five scenes: choose a copy, stop at a real barrier, use the detour bridge, compare the missing crossing, return current evidence without changing the old original. Missing bridge is a present observation, not a proven dated demolition or map authorship claim.

Fifteen new meanings:11 reserved +4 open slots inside unchanged21 ceiling. Existing forms/senses/cards keep first dates. New negative/plain surfaces are explicitly dated in delta. No new kanji glyph; familiar spellings retain authored readings.

Five sections each with two five-response sets;8A+8B+6C=72responses and13models. English cues disambiguate bank meanings. Full source, keys, readings, continuity and substantive licensing require independent review; checker alone does not prove naturalness.
Prior coverage remains an unchanged advisory; supplied English meanings precede first use and furigana supports decoding only. Continuity entries merge only at finalized release.

English instruction vocabulary extended only with the actual English teaching/cue words. No new Japanese instruction or grammar exception is inferred. Native SVGs are schematic fictional relationships; no coast geography claimed.
